role: Command-line front end of the code map: check (the CI gate, including the dependency re-check and, when the local findings overlay exists, the open-findings ratchet), status, sync, stamp, impact, callers and report. Run by scripts/check_codemap.sh, the codemap-* Makefile targets and the gates.yml impact step.
state: ROOT: repository root (two levels above this file)
OVERLAY: the local, untracked findings overlay, $CODEMAP_OVERLAY or do_not_ship/codemap under ROOT
FLAGS: OVERLAY/flags, one <path>.json per record holding {"file": [...], "units": {key: [...]}}
toplevel: Module docstring (the usage text main prints, including where the findings overlay lives), imports (collections, hashlib, json, os, subprocess, sys, Path), ROOT, RECORDS, OVERLAY and FLAGS, and sys.path insertion of scripts/codemap so inventory, graph and report import. `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main(argv))`.

units.does: Path of the record for a source path: RECORDS/<path>.json.

Attaches the overlay's findings to a parsed record: when FLAGS/<file>.json exists, sets the record's `flags` to its `file` list and each unit's `flags` to its entry under `units` (empty list when none). With no overlay file the record is returned unchanged, without `flags`. Returns the same dict.

branches.cond: overlay file for this record exists
branches.effect: file and unit flags attached; otherwise record unchanged

units.does: Reads and parses the record for a path and merges the overlay's findings into it (merge_flags); None when the record file does not exist.

Writes a record without findings: works on a deep copy, strips the file-level and unit `flags`, and writes the rest as indented UTF-8 JSON with a trailing newline to docs/codemap/records/<path>.json, creating directories as needed. Findings go only to the overlay: when any are present they are written to FLAGS/<path>.json as {"file": [...], "units": {key: [...]}} (creating the overlay directories); when none are present an existing overlay file for the record is deleted.

branches.cond: no findings and an overlay file exists

units.does: Walks RECORDS with os.walk (so hidden directories such as .github are included) and returns {source path: record} for every .json file, keyed by the record's own `file` field, with the overlay's findings merged into each (merge_flags).

Compares the inventory with the records and returns (path, key, message) for: a file with no record; a stale file hash; an empty role; a unit with no record; a unit record with empty `does`; a stale unit hash; a call to a `path::key` that is not a current unit (ext:/dyn:/closure: entries are not checked); a record for a unit no longer in the file; a record file for a path no longer in scope.

branches.effect: one problem; its units are not checked
problem; nothing else checked for it

branches.cond: call names a repo unit that is not in the current inventory
record keys with no matching unit
record files for paths not in scope

units.does: Hash (16 hex) of what a record says a unit does, the part callers rely on: for a unit its does, entry, reads, writes, and each branch's condition and effect; for a file record (file_level) its role, toplevel and state. Calls, hashes, evidence and findings (flags) are left out, so changing only how a unit is implemented, a branch's line offset, or the local findings overlay does not alter it. None gives ''.

branches.effect: role, toplevel, state; otherwise the unit fields

units.does: described() for every file record (node `path::`) and every unit record (`path::key`).
The record for a node: the file record for `path::`, otherwise the unit record with that key; None when either is missing.

branches.cond: file has no record, or the node is a file node

units.does: For a node, {callee: described hash} over its certain graph edges, sorted; a callee without a record maps to ''. This is what stamp stores as `deps` and what the re-check compares against.

branches.effect: included; possible edges are left out

units.does: For every file record and unit record whose code hash is current, compares its stored `deps` with current_deps: a certain callee missing from deps gives 're-check: now resolves a call to X, which it was not checked against'; a callee whose described hash differs gives 're-check: X changed what it does since this record was checked'. Stale records are skipped (the stale line already sends them back). Records with deps entries for callees no longer called are not reported.
Counts findings by severity (high/med/low) across every file-level and unit-level flag in all records. Flags with any other severity are not counted.

branches.cond: severity is high, med or low

units.does: Returns no problems when the findings overlay directory (OVERLAY) does not exist. Otherwise, for high and med: reads OVERLAY/codemap_open_<sev>.txt as an integer and reports a problem (path given relative to the repository root, key "open-findings ratchet") when the open count exceeds it (a change added findings) or is below it (a fix landed without lowering the budget). A missing or non-integer budget file inside an existing overlay is itself a problem, so the ratchet fails closed there.

branches.cond: budget file unreadable or not an integer
more open findings than the budget
fewer open findings than the budget
branches.effect: problem: lower the budget to the new count

units.does: Loads all records (with the overlay's findings when present), builds the inventory and the call graph. Failing problems: problems() except 'calls a unit that no longer exists', plus the open-findings ratchet (budget_problems over open_findings, which runs only when the overlay exists). Advisory (reported, never failing; a TODO(codemap-recheck) comment says to make them fail again once the outstanding re-check lines have been re-read): those stale-call lines plus dependency_problems() re-check lines. Prints the advisory count, and for `status` lists them grouped by file. No failing problems: prints success, and when the overlay exists also the open high/medium/low counts, and returns 0. Otherwise prints the failing problems grouped by file with how to fix each kind, and returns 1 for `check` (strict) or 0 for `status`.
Prints (path, key, message) items grouped by path: the path, then each key (or '(file record)') with its message, indented.

For each given path: if it is not in scope or untracked, deletes its record and its overlay findings file if a record exists (or says to git add it); otherwise loads (with findings) or creates the file record, keeps unit records whose key still exists in code order, adds empty records (hash null) for new units, drops records for units no longer in the code, and saves (findings to the overlay only). Never stamps a hash, so the new records fail check until written and stamped.

branches.cond: path not tracked or out of scope
branches.effect: removes an existing record, or prints a hint

branches.cond: record for a unit no longer present

units.does: Marks records as written against the current code. Builds the full inventory; refuses (2) when the path is out of scope or has no record. With no keys: refuses (1) if the file record's role is empty, else stores the current file hash and, as `deps`, current_deps of the file node from a freshly built graph. With keys: refuses (2) on an unknown key and (1) on a unit with an empty `does`; otherwise stores each unit's current code hash and its current_deps. Saves the record. It reads nothing for correctness; it trusts that the record was rewritten.

branches.cond: out of scope or no record

units.does: Lists (node, 'new'|'changed'|'deleted') for every mapped unit or file-level code whose content differs from `base`. Takes the paths `git diff --name-only <base>` reports (working tree against base), and for each reads the record as it was at base (`git show base:docs/codemap/records/<path>.json`); since the gate passed at base, that record's hashes are base's code hashes. A path out of scope now: if it had a record at base, its file node and units are 'deleted'. Otherwise the file node is 'new' or 'changed' when its hash differs, and each unit is 'new', 'changed' or 'deleted' by key and hash. Exits with a message when the diff fails (unknown ref).

branches.effect: parsed; otherwise treated as empty (everything new)

branches.cond: path not in scope now (deleted, untracked or excluded)
branches.effect: reported only if base had a record
file node and its units reported deleted
file node new (no base hash) or changed

units.does: Prints, as Markdown, what a change can affect. Targets: the named `path::key` nodes, or changed_since(base) (base from `--base REF`, default origin/main). An unknown named node prints up to 15 nodes containing its short name and returns 2. For each target: what its record says it does; direct callers, certain listed in full and possible up to 40; a walk up certain callers that stops at tests and doc sections (collected) and collects every caller with an `entry` as a trigger (up to 80 listed); for unit targets, each store it reads or writes (prefix up to ' (') with how many other units read and write it and up to 12 of them; and the open flags on the target and its certain direct callers (present only when the local findings overlay is merged in). The same text is appended to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (up to 900,000 characters) when that is set. Returns 0.

branches.effect: base taken from the next argument

branches.cond: a named node is not in the graph
target has a record and still exists

branches.effect: collected as a test, not walked further
collected as a doc, not walked further
listed as a trigger; walk continues past it
text appended to the job summary

units.does: Prints each direct caller of one node with its edge kind (certain first, then possible, each sorted), or a hint about the key format when there are none. Returns 0.

Dispatches argv: no args or -h/--help prints the usage and returns 0; check -> strict check; status -> non-strict; sync PATH...; stamp PATH [KEY...]; impact [--base REF] [NODE...]; callers NODE; report OUTDIR -> report.build over all records. Anything else prints the usage to stderr and returns 2.
units.entry: python3 scripts/codemap/codemap.py <command> (check_codemap.sh, the codemap-* Makefile targets, the gates.yml impact step, by hand)
